overview.headline: Using price index changes to adjust payments for escalation

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the Consumer Price Index measures average change in prices for a market basket of goods and services.
keyPoints.quote: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the average change in the prices paid for a market basket of goods and services.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that escalation agreements adjust payments for changes in prices using the most widely used measure of price change.
keyPoints.quote: Escalation agreements often use the CPI—the most widely used measure of price change—to adjust payments for changes in prices.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that choosing a CPI series requires specifying population coverage, area coverage, series title, and index base period.
keyPoints.quote: population coverage (CPI-U or CPI-W), area coverage (U.S. City Average, West Region, Chicago, etc.)

keyPoints.point: Students learn that a cap places an upper limit on the increase while a floor promises a minimum increase regardless of CPI change.
keyPoints.quote: a “cap” that places an upper limit on the increase in wages, rents, etc., or a “floor” that promises a minimum increase

keyTerms.gloss: measure of average change in prices paid for a market basket of goods and services
keyTerms.quote: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the average change in the prices paid for a market basket of goods and services.

keyTerms.gloss: population group representing over 90 percent of urban families based on expenditures in urban areas
keyTerms.quote: The CPI-U represents over 90 percent of the total U.S. population and is based on the expenditures of all families living in urban areas.

keyTerms.gloss: subset of urban population based on expenditures of families living in urban areas
keyTerms.quote: The CPI-W is a subset of the CPI-U and is based on the expenditures of families living in urban areas

keyTerms.gloss: contract allowance that places an upper limit on the increase in wages and rents
keyTerms.quote: a “cap” that places an upper limit on the increase in wages, rents, etc., or a “floor” that promises a minimum increase

keyTerms.gloss: contract allowance that promises a minimum increase regardless of price change
keyTerms.quote: a “cap” that places an upper limit on the increase in wages, rents, etc., or a “floor” that promises a minimum increase
